reconstruction.text: Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner product space with its Borel measurable structure, μ a probability measure on E, and C a positive real number. Suppose that for every smooth compactly supported real-valued v on E, the integral of v² log(v²) minus the integral of v² times the logarithm of that integral is at most 2C times the integral of the squared norm of the gradient of v, with all integrals taken against μ. If a pair (f,w) in scalar and E-valued L²(μ), respectively, belongs to the joint norm closure of the pairs represented μ-almost everywhere by (g,∇g) for smooth compactly supported real-valued g on E, then the variance of f under μ is at most C times the squared L²(μ) norm of w.

On a finite-dimensional complete real Hilbert space E with its Borel structure, let μ be a probability measure and C>0 a fixed real. decoder_context: ContDiff real infinity means global smoothness. Compact support is compact closure of the nonzero set.

Lp with exponent two means equivalence classes of a.e. strongly measurable functions of finite square norm, modulo a.e. equality. The coercions to functions pick representatives. The product topology is the joint norm topology.

ProbabilityTheory.variance on an L² scalar is the real integral of its squared deviation from its mean. All scalar integrals are real Bochner integrals. The gradient is the actual Riesz gradient of the specified smooth representative.
The vector norm on an L² class is its usual L² norm; the set closure does not posit a single-valued linear map. Real.log at zero has value zero.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.CompactLogSobolevPoincare
import Mathlib.Probability.Moments.Variance

/-!
# Poincaré on the closure of the compact gradient pairs

An explicit Euclidean graph-closure step for Chewi, *Log-Concave Sampling*,
Exercise 1.7 and the density discussion in §2.1.1. This does not assume or
prove single-valuedness of the closure for an arbitrary measure.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.CompactGradientPoincareClosure

open MeasureTheory InnerProductSpace
open scoped ContDiff RealInnerProductSpace

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [CompleteSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [MeasurableSpace E] [BorelSpace E]

/-- Compact smooth LSI gives the same-constant variance bound on the joint
`L² × L²` closure of the original compact smooth function/gradient pairs. -/
theorem poincare_of_compact_logSobolev_on_gradient_closure
    (μ : Measure E) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 < C)
    (hLSI : ∀ v : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ v → HasCompactSupport v →
      (∫ x, (v x)^2 * Real.log ((v x)^2) ∂μ) -
        (∫ x, (v x)^2 ∂μ) * Real.log (∫ x, (v x)^2 ∂μ) ≤
      2 * C * ∫ x, ‖gradient v x‖^2 ∂μ)
    (p : Lp ℝ 2 μ × Lp E 2 μ)
    (hp : p ∈ closure {r | ∃ g : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ g ∧ HasCompactSupport g ∧
        r.1 =ᵐ[μ] g ∧ r.2 =ᵐ[μ] gradient g}) :
    ProbabilityTheory.variance (p.1 : E → ℝ) μ ≤ C * ‖p.2‖^2 := by
  have norm_sq (z : Lp E 2 μ) : ‖z‖^2 = ∫ x, ‖z x‖^2 ∂μ := by
    rw [← real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, L2.inner_def]
    simp only [real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
  have hone : MemLp (fun _ : E => (1 : ℝ)) 2 μ := memLp_const 1
  let one := hone.toLp (fun _ : E => (1 : ℝ))
  have mean (a : Lp ℝ 2 μ) : inner ℝ one a = ∫ x, a x ∂μ := by
    rw [L2.inner_def]
    apply integral_congr_ae
    filter_upwards [hone.coeFn_toLp] with x hx
    change inner ℝ (one x) (a x) = a x
    rw [show one x = 1 from hx]
    simp
  have var (a : Lp ℝ 2 μ) :
      ProbabilityTheory.variance (a : E → ℝ) μ = ‖a‖^2 - (inner ℝ one a)^2 := by
    have ha : ‖a‖^2 = ∫ x, (a x)^2 ∂μ := by
      rw [← real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, L2.inner_def]
      simp only [real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs]
    rw [ProbabilityTheory.variance_eq_sub (Lp.memLp a), mean, ha]
    rfl
  let S : Set (Lp ℝ 2 μ × Lp E 2 μ) :=
    {r | ProbabilityTheory.variance (r.1 : E → ℝ) μ ≤ C * ‖r.2‖^2}
  have hS : IsClosed S := by
    dsimp only [S]
    simp_rw [var]
    exact isClosed_le
      ((continuous_fst.norm.pow 2).sub ((continuous_const.inner continuous_fst).pow 2))
      (continuous_const.mul (continuous_snd.norm.pow 2))
  have hcompact : {r : Lp ℝ 2 μ × Lp E 2 μ | ∃ g : E → ℝ,
      ContDiff ℝ ∞ g ∧ HasCompactSupport g ∧ r.1 =ᵐ[μ] g ∧
      r.2 =ᵐ[μ] gradient g} ⊆ S := by
    rintro ⟨a, b⟩ ⟨g, hg, hgc, ha, hb⟩
    change ProbabilityTheory.variance (a : E → ℝ) μ ≤ C * ‖b‖^2
    have henergy : (∫ x, ‖b x‖^2 ∂μ) = ∫ x, ‖gradient g x‖^2 ∂μ :=
      integral_congr_ae (hb.mono fun _ hx => congrArg (fun v : E => ‖v‖^2) hx)
    rw [ProbabilityTheory.variance_congr ha,
      ProbabilityTheory.variance_eq_integral hg.continuous.measurable.aemeasurable,
      norm_sq b, henergy]
    exact CompactLogSobolevPoincare.poincare_of_compact_logSobolev μ C hC hLSI g hg hgc
  exact closure_minimal hcompact hS hp

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.FunctionalInequalities.CompactGradientPoincareClosure

steps.title: Make variance continuous on L²
steps.text: The mean is pairing with the constant-one L² class. On a probability measure, variance is the squared L² norm minus the square of this mean. Both pieces are continuous in the scalar L² norm.
steps.lean: mean uses L2.inner_def and a.e. equality of the constant representative; var uses variance_eq_sub and the real squared norm identity.

steps.title: Prove the inequality on the actual test pairs
steps.text: Take a pair represented by g and its true gradient. Use a.e. invariance of variance and the vector L² norm formula, then the prior compact-test PI obtained from LSI. No hypothesis about the resulting inequality is added.
steps.lean: hcompact invokes the actual compact LSI-to-PI parent, with variance_congr and the integral_congr_ae energy identity.

steps.title: Pass closed order to joint limits
steps.text: The inequality defines a closed subset of the product because both sides are continuous. Since it contains all compact pairs, it contains their closure. No limit is required to be a classical derivative or a single-valued graph for an arbitrary law.
steps.formula: G\subseteq S=\{(u,H):\operatorname{Var}_\mu(u)\le C\|H\|_2^2\},\quad S\text{ closed}\ \Longrightarrow\ \overline G\subseteq S.
steps.lean: hS is isClosed_le on the scalar and vector expressions; closure_minimal supplies the conclusion.

steps.title: Check the actual Gibbs consumer
steps.text: For a normalized Gibbs measure with C¹ potential and integrable exponential weight, the existing construction produces a closable compact-gradient map. For a C¹ observable with f and its gradient both in L²(μ), the existing C¹-domain theorem places their classes in that very graph closure. The focused test applies the bound there from the given compact LSI, without assuming PI, curvature, an extra law-tail moment, or a graph-membership certificate.
steps.lean: The test consumes compact_gradient_closable, c1_in_closed_gradient and graph_closure_eq_closure_graph, then unfolds the same two norm/variance quantities. The compact LSI premise is still given.

lesson.lean_statement: The candidate pair belongs to the actual joint closure of compact smooth representative pairs; the norm of its vector component is the energy.
lesson.lean_proof: Use the variance identity and the closed inequality set; feed the existing compact PI bound to closure_minimal. No artificial sequence, assumed approximation estimate, or operator closability enters the proof.
